decision_scope: Complete cross-repository technical content and final candidate CI. Actual wrapper acceptance, exact attestation integrity and merged-source rebinding are separately required subsequent records; this is not a claim that those uninspected records have already passed.

subject_coverage.verification: All 87 actual scoped decisions were independently run through verify_scoped_review. Their complete reviewed pin sets form 706 unique paths; every hash equals the corresponding frozen Git blob and overlapping pins have no conflict. This report deliberately contains no contract_reviews or task_reviews arrays.

independence.statement: The overall review integrates the three completed independent domain reviews and independently checks cross-repository coherence, evidence, ownership, documentation and workflow. It does not manufacture another domain decision or a GitHub account endorsement.

completeness.interpretation: Coverage categories state design support relative to the named feature families. Limited, planned and unsupported rows remain visible and do not become implemented functionality merely because upstream Rust or .NET exposes it.

cross_repository_conclusions.conclusion: The design consistently keeps database drivers, query AST/dialects/relations/execution and Server network/protocol/runtime work in mandatory mature Rust Engines. C# owns strongly typed application composition, static descriptors, serializers, materializers and handlers. Kestrel and managed database libraries are comparators. The final Server, Database, Core contracts and all 48 future task responsibilities agree; there is no managed SQL/network fallback or mandatory global Core runtime.

cross_repository_conclusions.area: Complete public API and native mapping
cross_repository_conclusions.conclusion: The compiled declarations, per-type semantic policies, operation tables and feature matrices form one coherent design authority. Exact signatures, generic constraints, nullable/default semantics, overload limits, ownership, error/cancellation behavior, capability restrictions and cost profiles are documented. Domain reviewers independently closed concrete mapping omissions, including relation transport, nullable SQL lifting, HTTP completion, binary gRPC metadata, MCP gate continuation and retained-byte admission.

cross_repository_conclusions.area: Ordinary C# consumption and Native AOT
cross_repository_conclusions.conclusion: Minimal and advanced consumers use natural factories/builders, typed columns/Fluent operations, static JSON/protobuf/handler metadata, normal Task/async enumeration and ordinary disposal. Default provider/Server packages carry the intended generator/native dependencies. An ordinary Entity/DTO/Handler edit rebuilds managed output while retaining precompiled native bytes; no user Rust build, rd.xml, reflection-preservation list or runtime expression compiler is required by the design. The handwritten static seam is explicit and is assigned parity tests.

Core is BCL-only and starts no runtime by itself. Database providers and Server are independently consumable; Query is a namespace in the Database assembly to avoid a cycle. Optional DI/Hosting/gRPC/MCP packages extend the same owners. One Server native module with optional protocol code has an explicit binary-size cost and does not introduce a second runtime or listener. DI root ownership, lazy request scopes, frozen configuration and same-host protocol lifetime are coherent.

Managed task completion, native terminal result, owner release, callback quiescence, transport end and thread join remain different observations. Retained native/managed capacities stay charged until their true last owner. Server payload credit has no wait/retry cycle; queue/network waits are separately bounded. Unknown transaction outcomes remain unknown despite cancellation or cleanup. Response/protocol terminals and failure-isolated cleanup preserve exactly-once dispatch and release rules.

Finite route/binder/schema/header/body budgets, trusted-proxy processing, wire Host/Origin separation, explicit auth seams, MCP pre-parse authorization for automatic and business methods, gRPC framed denial, TLS capability/configuration and redacted diagnostics are specified together. Static root/nullability restrictions and no-reflection fallbacks are explicit. These are reviewed design constraints, not a claim of product security testing.

The standard and documentation system require XML, exact generated reference, guides, examples, compatibility review and real consumer/AOT evidence as part of each implementing task. Every one of the 48 Delivery tasks has exact API inputs and a documentation owner; all ten fragments mirror that task system without a new scheduling graph. A13 supplies shared build enforcement, A22 compatibility policy, A24 scaffold adoption and A16/B24 final package composition. New repositories must explicitly pin/adopt the standard; AGENTS links do not imply inheritance.

The standard version is 1.0.0, distinct from the 0.4.0 contract/document/task refinement. Native source, C ABI, managed API/package and domain semantics are separately versioned. Source/binary/default/nullability/disposal changes require review and migration; future compatibility baselines cannot silently accept removals or behavioral changes.

Preserved source readings, finite models, actual native research, compiled declarations, static AOT fixture execution and future product gates retain separate labels. Historical accepted files are preserved; old translation or research acceptance is not reused as approval of new API bytes. No upstream whole-suite read/run, production workload, whole-process RSS bound or near-native performance winner is invented.

The reviewed workflow now binds normative support files and enforcement/adoption rules, complete required paths, task semantic digests, actual reports and attributable exact wrapper attestations. It preserves earlier accepted snapshots. The correct sequence is fresh contract preparation and independent attestation, contract acceptance, fresh task preparation and attestation, complete accepted-state checks, final candidate review, one PR per repository, Design merge first, byte comparison plus fresh merged-source task bindings and same-reviewer attestations in the same Plan PR, then final checks/review before Plan merge. No source rebind inherits acceptance automatically.
